transcript:
Header: 2025-11-19 15:00 UTC | Duration 38m | Recording ID ff-20251119-nebula-0457
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Samir (CSM) — Aria (CTO), Ethan (ML Eng), Priya (Platform), Marcus (SRE), J. Park (Procurement)

00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check in — we'll run through access, infra readiness, and the perf notes from last run. Samir?
00:18 Samir: yep, quick housekeeping, thanks for the updated creds yesterday. i saw that the storage keys were rotated, all good there.
00:30 Aria: thanks — we got most things in, still blocked on the VPC peering request, looks like networking team needs the peering CIDR.
00:42 Maya: ok we'll re-share the peering template. Priya, can you paste the peering request id in chat after?
00:56 Priya: yes i'll drop it, just need the exact egress IP range for the bastion so we can whitelist.
01:08 Jonah: on the perf side, we re-ran the 2.5B baseline with your sample workload. tail latency spiked at 780ms at 95th with current batching of 8 and no KV warmup. if we enable prefix KV warmup and bump to batching 12 the model reduced 95th to ~520ms but token cost went up ~8%.
01:34 Ethan: ok that's helpful; our SLA target is 600ms p95 max for user-facing recommendations. 8% cost is ok if latency is within SLA.
01:46 Jonah: yeah so trade-off seems acceptable. also note we saw several cold-start effects on first 30s of run — KV cache miss rate was high. warming the KV cache via synthetic prefix requests solved that for the run.
02:05 Marcus: how invasive is the warming? we worry about extra compute during warmup impacting other jobs.
02:16 Jonah: minimal — it's a short burst, think of it as a 2-5 minute lightweight fanout. can be scheduled during maintenance windows or as part of canary.
02:32 Aria: any redwood dedicated options? we're evaluating Dedicated vs hosted; security favors Dedicated but cost team is nervous.
02:44 Maya: totally — we can propose a Dedicated configuration with reserved capacity; there are autoscale burst options. we also have private deployment (VPC + private control plane) for regulated data, which addresses audit/KMS concerns.
02:58 J. Park: on procurement timeline, we need SOC2 docs and network diagrams to share with legal; can you resend those?
03:10 Samir: yes we'll email SOC2 packet and the network diagram today, and include the KMS integration note.
03:22 Ethan: quick q on model variants — you suggested a quantized 4-bit trial, is that compatible with our sequence lengths (avg 280 tokens)?
03:36 Jonah: for 4-bit quant we saw a slight fuzz on some NER edge cases; for 280 avg seq it's generally fine but we should run a small eval set. we'll pair quant recommendation with eval pass to check quality delta.
03:52 Priya: for access we have the bastion up but need the public IP whitelist; i'll add the screenshot to the ticket after this call.
04:06 Maya: perfect. next, can we align on the canary run scope — recommended: 10k messages, 48-hour window, steady ramp to 30 RPS, measure p50/p95/p99 and token cost. any objections?
04:28 Ethan: sounds reasonable, want to include a small set of golden prompts for quality gating too.
04:40 Jonah: will add that, and include the KV-cache warmup script in the playbook.
04:52 Aria: timeline? once peering + whitelist done we can run next week.
05:00 Maya: ok target: run canary starting 2025-11-26. Redwood to share playbook and benchmark sheet by 2025-11-21.
05:12 Marcus: any special notes about our k8s cluster — we run mixed node pools, so bursting to GPUs may schedule pods unevenly.
05:24 Jonah: noted, we'll include scheduling guidance; for Dedicated we recommend pinned instances to avoid preemption jitter.
05:34 Priya: one small nit — in your earlier doc you mentioned KV "cash" and we thought that was a billing note, ha — typos in autogenerated doc confused a few folks.
05:48 Maya: yeah apologies, fireflies transcription and a few typos slipped in. we'll send clean doc.
06:00 J. Park: procurement question: is there a minimum commitment for Dedicated?
06:12 Maya: yes Dedicated has monthly reserved tiers; we'll include options in the pricing deck.
06:22 Ethan: for the bench runs, what's the recommended client timeout? we currently set 2s which caused retries in the last run.
06:36 Jonah: increase to 6s for heavy LLM paths, or use client-side hedging with shorter timeout but multiple replicas — we'll recommend config.
06:50 Aria: ok wrapping up, any other blockers?
06:56 Priya: VPC peering + bastion whitelist are the only infra blocks.
07:02 Maya: great, we'll follow up with the benchmark CSV, playbook, SOC2 and network diagram today. can we reconvene next Tuesday quick sync?
07:12 Aria: yes that works. thanks all.
07:18 End of recording.
